test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 27 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Many unicellular algae like Chlamydomonas live in water. How do they take in oxygen for respiration?

options.text: They absorb dissolved oxygen via diffusion like Amoeba.
They have tiny openings (spiracles) to take in gases.
They store oxygen evolved via photosynthesis in their vacuoles.

solution:
The correct answer is __**They absorb dissolved oxygen via diffusion like Amoeba**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Unicellular algae like **Chlamydomonas absorb dissolved oxygen in water via diffusion, similar to Amoeba.** 
 
• Chlamydomonas is a** unicellular green algae that can survive in both aerobic and anaerobic environments**.
 
• It performs** photosynthesis in chloroplasts and aerobic respiration in mitochondria**
 
• Chlamydomonas** is a typical photoautotroph**, using the energy of sunlight to synthesize c**arbohydrates from carbon dioxide/bicarbonate ion and water and then using the carbohydrates as a both an energy source in cellular respiration and also as building materials to synthesize a variety of biomolecules.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/10e6a4767cea3ed85ea643f1afbe06be69ccd27e08307bf1e6e6b2e8e739e705.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Chlamydomonas
 
• It is a genus of unicellular green algae (Chlorophyta).
 
• It is found in soil, stagnant water, and freshwater.
 
• Palmella stage is a type of asexual reproduction found in some algae such as mainly in Chlamydomonas, Euglena, etc.
 
• The palmella stage is formed under unfavorable conditions as a shortage of water, excess salts, etc.
 
• Green algae, variable in size and shape, include single-celled (Chlamydomonas, desmids), colonial (Hydrodictyon, Volvox), filamentous (Spirogyra, Cladophora), and tubular (Actebularia, Caulerpa) forms.
 
• Sexual reproduction is common, with gametes that have two or four flagella.
 
 
• The golden-brown algae and diatoms are the most widespread unicellular species of algae.
 
• Some examples are amoeba, paramecium, bacteria, and cyanobacteria.
